game: MIA@MIN Week 4 2026 (kickoff time not in pack; spread/total not saved; weather not saved)

script.base: No saved spread, so this is not a priced blowout. The pack's defining fact is Minnesota's 73% blitz against a Miami dropback game that is -0.26 EPA/db when blitzed and +0.06 when not. Base flow: messy, lower-efficiency, not a shootout. Miami's vertical shots (Malik Washington 275 air yards on 23 targets; Chris Bell 180 air on 10) are the casualties; Greg Dulcich (12 targets, 68 air, TE) and Malik Willis's legs (17 carries, 101 yards) are the outlets. Minnesota, with Justin Jefferson out (17 targets, 179 yards), leans on Aaron Jones (52 carries, 203 yards) plus a redistributed pass game to Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson rather than a track meet.
script.flip1: Miami falls behind, abandons Ollie Gordon/De'Von Achane, and Willis is spied into sacks instead of scrambles (his 6-yard rush game is the template). If the 73% blitz does not actually get home, Washington/Bell explosives still cash — Minnesota has allowed 12 passes of 20+ — and the checkdown/QB-run story dies.
script.flip2: Miami leads and clocks out with Achane (34 carries, 127 yards) and Willis designed runs. Dulcich and the other pass overs stall. The other side of that flip: Jefferson-less Minnesota trails and throws, so Jones's rush dies and Addison/Hockenson volume rises.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game outs only. MIN WR Justin Jefferson Out (ankle) vacates 17 targets/179 yards/189 air; same-position heirs are Addison (already 16 targets/111/221 air), then Hockenson (13/76/93), Josh Oliver (5/46, no prop), Jauan Jennings (3/1), Tai Felton (2/0), and Jones (7 targets/34 yards). MIA WR Caleb Douglas Out (ankle) vacates 10 targets/113 yards/114 air; next men already producing are Washington (23/152), Dulcich (12/90), Bell (10/92), with Keon Coleman (6 targets, 3 yards) and Ryan Miller (4 targets, 92 yards) as low-share options. MIA CB Storm Duck Out (knee) and MIA LB Rob Beal Jr. Out (hamstring) are coverage losses that help MIN WRs/TE/RB, not Miami skill players. MIN CB Charles Demmings Out (hamstring) is a corner absence (starter vs depth not in pack) that mildly helps MIA WRs. MIN P Brett Thorson Out has no prop impact. Achane is not listed out. Sources: pack injury report plus weeks 1-3 target/rush totals.

matchup.shell: Man/zone and MOFO/MOFC not charted (step 4 limited). Location proxy only: MIN allows left 7.11 YPA (37 att), middle 10.04 (28), right 5.25 (48) — middle is the open area, right is the strength side. MIA allows left 8.62 (26), middle 10.57 (23), right 8.37 (27), soft on every side.
matchup.pressure: MIN blitz rate 73%; MIA EPA/db -0.26 vs blitz and +0.06 vs no blitz. That is the game's pressure edge. MIA blitzes only 32%; MIN EPA/db -0.22 vs blitz and 0.00 vs no blitz, so Minnesota is not facing the same heat.
matchup.bleeds: MIN bleeds the middle (10.04 YPA) and has allowed 12 passes of 20+ (127); it does not bleed the run (3.52 YPC, 8 runs of 10+). MIA bleeds the middle worst (10.57) and is soft left and right, with 9 passes of 20+ (76) and a solid-not-elite 3.82 YPC allowed (9 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Dulcich, the short/intermediate TE (68 air on 12 targets), into MIN's middle bleed plus the blitz-checkdown funnel. Bell (18.0 air yards/target) and Washington (12.0) overlap the area pressure should kill, but MIN's 12 explosives mean that overlap is incomplete. Addison overlaps Duck's absence and MIA's soft YPA, but 62.5 already sits ~25 above his 37 ypg.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Minnesota blitzes 73% and Miami drops to -0.26 EPA/db against the blitz, which funnels throws to Dulcich (12 targets, 90 yards, only 68 air) in the middle where Minnesota allows 10.04 YPA, and Douglas's 10 vacated targets add volume a 29.5 line set on his 30-yard mean does not fully price.
edge_players.must_be_true: Dulcich plays his normal snap/route share, the blitz produces checkdowns rather than only sacks and throwaways, and he gets a slice of Douglas's 10 targets instead of all of them sticking with Washington.
edge_players.kills_it: The 18- and 17-yard games are the real role and the 55 was a fluke; Washington/Bell absorb Douglas; or Miami leads and clocks out with Achane and Willis so the TE never sees a fourth target.

data_check.notes: No sims, no projection file, and no Pinnacle — anchor is consensus no-vig. Step 8 cannot be run for real, so this is a flag, not an agree. Dulcich raw hit rate vs 29.5 is 1/3 (18, 17, 55); the 0.58 is a scheme-adjusted hand estimate, not a sim, and 70%+ would be untrustworthy anyway. Willis raw rate vs 30.5 is 2/3 with mean 33.7, which agrees in direction, but MIN 3.52 YPC disagrees and n=3. Dropped, not selected: Washington rec under 40.5 (scheme fits, but floor is 43 and Douglas Out adds targets — counter-case stronger); Bell rec under 34.5 (18.0 aDOT fits the blitz, but 67-yard game, 12 explosives allowed, Demmings Out, and Douglas's 10 targets are a stronger counter on a lean); Addison 62.5 and Hockenson 38.5 look already repriced for Jefferson and were not average-chased; Wright rush 27.5 vs -1/11 conflicts with a 0.502 over no-vig, so the market is telling a role story this report does not confirm. No leg is short of -250. Do not size either lean/strong off a hand p.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Dulcich finished 17-18 yards because the 73% blitz produced sacks and throwaways, not checkdowns, Washington kept the 23-target share plus Douglas's routes, and 55 yards was the outlier the line had already respected by sitting on 29.5. Willis finished at 6 again because Minnesota's 3.52 YPC front and a spy took away the edge, and a coin-flip -113 number had no cushion once the designed runs were bottled. The same pack that builds the blitz story also holds the counters: two quiet Dulcich games, one dead Willis game, no saved spread to prove Miami will be throwing, and no sim that beat the no-vig by a real 3 points.
slip_story: One story only: Minnesota's blitz script. Stack is Dulcich recyds over (middle/checkdown) with Willis rushyds over (escape lanes). Do not add Washington or Bell overs, a game-total over, Gordon rush over, or the Jefferson-out Minnesota pass overs (Addison 62.5, Hockenson 38.5) — those need the blitz to fail or a different script. Bell under was the correlated deep-shot fade and was left off because Douglas Out makes that under the wrong side of the same injury. No TDs, one market per player, two legs, not a bet placement.
